FLASHCARD SET · AGES 3–4 YEARS

Body Parts & Five Senses Flashcards for Preschoolers

Twenty-four cards about the one thing your child knows best: their own body. Every card has its own page with the picture, the words to say together and one thing to try — from wiggling fingers to sniffing flowers.

THE CARDS

Every card in the set.

Each card has its own page: the picture and short, practical notes for grown-ups — what it is for, how to use it, how to print it. Tap any card to open it.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Name it, then touch it

    The pair is the whole lesson: “head!” — then both hands on your head. Saying the word while feeling the body part wires them together, and the touching is the fun half.

  2. 02

    Play the pointing game backwards

    Once a few cards feel easy, your child names a body part and YOU point. Getting one wrong on purpose — pointing at your elbow when they say nose — keeps the game alive for weeks.

  3. 03

    Follow one sense all day

    Pick a sense card at breakfast and be its helper all morning: ears day, nose day, fingers day. One sense at a time is how the five of them become friends.

  4. 04

    Take one card on the road

    Tape the hands card by the sink or the look card by the window. Every hand-wash and every “what do you see?” becomes a quiet repetition — and repetitions are what make the words stick.

      Head Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Your child has known their head since they first shook it to say no. On this card the word head sits under a smiling boy, ready for a game you can play without any props at all.

      What this card names

      Names the headquarters everything else lives under, printed where a finger can land.

      Use it right now

      Rest one warm hand flat on top and feel the thinking happen.

      What your child picks up

      Body-map basics: every face part gets an address once named.

      Print it like this

      Print portrait, one per page — heads deserve the space.

      Grown-up tip

      Measure your child's head against the card — growth is suddenly official.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Head lesson on the Learning Path.

      Eyes Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Two eyes, always working: watching the dog, finding the lost sock, reading the pictures. This card pairs the word eyes with a close-up pair of brown ones — very probably blinking right now.

      What this card names

      Covers both the seeing and the showing-off — blinks, winks, wide looks.

      Use it right now

      Wink twice at dinner — one eye only, then admire the attempt.

      What your child picks up

      Attention becomes deliberate once the tool doing it has a name.

      Print it like this

      Ordinary paper works; eyes survive all printers.

      Grown-up tip

      Copy their wink back badly; failed winks are bonding.

      Teach it, step by step
